notes: THREE LICENCE SURFACES, NOT ONE. The GLM-OCR checkpoint is MIT (model card + license:mit tag). The official SDK github.com/zai-org/GLM-OCR is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE present; pyproject license text Apache-2.0). The SDK's pipeline additionally downloads PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors for layout analysis, which is Apache-2.0 and is a separate model with a separate card. The card says so itself: 'Users should comply with both licenses.' license.id here names the model; the other two are pinned in inference_config and named in official_source_urls so no surface is cleared by accident. None of this settles patent FTO for any of them.

OFFICIAL PATH: the model card says 'For document parsing tasks, we strongly recommend using our official SDK', because the SDK is what adds PP-DocLayoutV3 layout analysis and parallel region OCR on top of the raw model. Running the checkpoint alone with a bare 'Text Recognition:' prompt would be a materially weaker configuration than the one the vendor benchmarks, and masterplan 6.2 allows each model its own official recommended path. This runtime therefore drives glmocr==0.1.5 in self-hosted mode against a local vLLM server.

PROMPTS: the SDK's page_loader.task_prompt_mapping is {text: 'Text Recognition:', table: 'Table Recognition:', formula: 'Formula Recognition:'} and the model card's 'Prompt Limited' section says those are the only document-parsing prompts the model supports. prompt_id glm_ocr_official_sdk_task_prompts_v1 registers that mapping plus the SDK revision, not one string. Information-extraction JSON-schema prompts are out of scope for this campaign.

SAMPLING is the SDK's own default block (glmocr/config.yaml, pipeline.page_loader): max_tokens 8192, temperature 0.0, top_p 1e-05, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.1, min_pixels 12544, max_pixels 71372800, image_expect_length 6144, image_format JPEG. Changed on purpose: retry_max_attempts 2 -> 0, because retries belong to the controller (masterplan 15.9), and maas.enabled true -> false, because MaaS mode would send the founder's pages to Zhipu's hosted API instead of running the open model. max_workers 32 -> 8 because the arena serves one page at a time per adapter call.

VERSION PINS THE OFFICIAL DOCS EXPRESS AS FLOORS: the model card's vLLM snippet says 'pip install -U vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly', and the SDK README says 'pip install -U "vllm>=0.17.0"' or 'docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-ubuntu2404'. A nightly wheel cannot be pinned and 'no pip install -U' is a hard rule (masterplan 15.1), so the base image is the SDK's own recommended tag taken by digest, and torch/vLLM are pinned by that digest rather than reinstalled. transformers is the one exception, and it is pinned explicitly rather than asserted -- see the next note.

TRANSFORMERS PIN 5.3.0, and the claim this note replaces was false. The earlier text said 'the build asserts the image's transformers is >= 5.3.0 and fails if it is not'. bootstrap.sh asserted nothing; it only recorded versions. On 2026-09-03 pod 92miysvw0wk4wq (RTX 4090) the bootstrap completed -- bundle sha verified, glmocr==0.1.5 installed, both checkpoints verified -- and then vllm serve died in 10 s on a pydantic ValidationError for ModelConfig: the checkpoint's model_type glm_ocr was unknown to the transformers in vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-ubuntu2404. RunPod restarted the exited start command, so the pod billed a GPU in an invisible crash loop. vLLM 0.19.0 does implement the architecture: model_executor/models/registry.py maps GlmOcrForConditionalGeneration -> ('glm_ocr', ...) and GlmOcrMTPModel -> ('glm_ocr_mtp', ...) for the MTP speculative head, and its own glm_ocr.py imports transformers.models.glm_ocr.configuration_glm_ocr, so its declared 'transformers >= 4.56.0, < 5' in requirements/common.txt is stale against its own code. The SDK README's 'Using vLLM' section resolves it on this exact image tag with 'pip install "transformers>=5.3.0"'. That is a floor, and masterplan 15.1 forbids floors, so a pin is what ships. The pin was 5.3.0 -- the SDK's stated floor, released 2026-03-04, a month before vLLM 0.19.0 (2026-04-03) -- until the 2026-09-04 read showed the SDK's own layout stage needs 5.4.0; see the next note.

THE PIN IS 5.4.0, AND 5.3.0 -- THE VERSION THE VENDOR NAMES -- WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED. The SDK README says 'pip install "transformers>=5.3.0"', and the earlier pass turned that floor into transformers==5.3.0. Reading the SDK's own layout stage on 2026-09-04 showed the floor is wrong against its own code: glmocr/layout/layout_detector.py does 'from transformers import PPDocLayoutV3ForObjectDetection, PPDocLayoutV3ImageProcessor' at module level, and at transformers v5.3.0 the second name does not exist. v5.3.0 ships image_processing_pp_doclayout_v3_fast.py whose __all__ is ['PPDocLayoutV3ImageProcessorFast'], and image_processing_auto.py maps ('pp_doclayout_v3', (None, 'PPDocLayoutV3ImageProcessorFast')) -- a null slow slot, so there is no alias to fall back on. v5.4.0 (2026-03-27) is the first release where the file is image_processing_pp_doclayout_v3.py and __all__ carries the un-suffixed name; v5.5.0, v5.6.0, v5.8.0 and v5.16.1 carry it too, and src/transformers/models/glm_ocr/ is still present at v5.4.0, so model_type glm_ocr is unaffected. THIS FAILURE WAS INVISIBLE TO THE ARCHITECTURE PREFLIGHT: glmocr/layout/__init__.py catches the ImportError, sets PPDocLayoutDetector = None and re-raises only when Pipeline() is built -- inside the worker, on a billed GPU. The import preflight added to bootstrap.sh imports glmocr.layout.layout_detector directly, as a leaf, so the SDK's own guard cannot mask it.

WHY NOT THE NEWEST TRANSFORMERS. 5.16.1 was the newest on PyPI on 2026-09-03. It requires tokenizers >=0.23.1,<0.24 and safetensors >=0.8.0; transformers 5.4.0 requires tokenizers >=0.22.0,<=0.23.0 and safetensors >=0.4.3. The pod carries safetensors 0.7.0, so the newest release would drag safetensors and tokenizers along underneath a vLLM that was built and CI-tested against transformers 4.57.5 / tokenizers 0.22.0. 5.4.0 forces exactly one upgrade: huggingface_hub, which every transformers 5.x requires at >= 1.3.0 (>= 1.5.0 from 5.4.0) while the pod log showed 0.36.2. Four pins, identical in bootstrap.sh and Dockerfile: transformers==5.4.0, tokenizers==0.22.2 (0.22.0 caps huggingface_hub at < 1.0 and cannot coexist with transformers 5.x; 0.22.2 allows < 2.0 and still satisfies vLLM's own 'tokenizers >= 0.21.1'), huggingface_hub==1.5.0 (exactly 5.4.0's new floor), hf-xet==1.3.2 (huggingface_hub 1.5.0 raises its floor from 1.1.3 to 1.2.0 and this lane has no evidence of the image's version). Installed with --no-deps so pip cannot resolve torch or vLLM again. The 5.3.0 -> 5.4.0 step moves exactly one bound, so the other three pins are unchanged rather than re-derived. NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE: no combination of vLLM 0.19.0 with any transformers 5.x is attested by a vendor receipt, huggingface_hub 0.36.2 -> 1.5.0 is a major version step underneath vLLM, and the upper end of the transformers window was not walked release by release -- 5.4.0 is the floor of the window, chosen over a newer release because every extra minor is more drift under a vLLM whose own metadata still says transformers < 5. The import and architecture preflights are what turn that residual risk into a fail-closed exit instead of a crash loop.

WORDFREQ IS AN UNDECLARED DEPENDENCY OF THE SDK, and it is on the self-hosted load path. glmocr/postprocess/result_formatter.py imports 'from wordfreq import zipf_frequency' at module level; glmocr/postprocess/__init__.py imports ResultFormatter with no try/except; glmocr/pipeline/pipeline.py imports 'from glmocr.postprocess import ResultFormatter'. The string wordfreq appears nowhere in glmocr 0.1.5's pyproject.toml -- not in the base dependencies, not in the selfhosted extra -- so 'pip install glmocr[selfhosted]' yields a package whose Pipeline cannot be constructed. wordfreq==3.1.1 is pinned in both bootstrap.sh and the Dockerfile, and it is the one pin installed WITH deps: msgpack, langcodes, ftfy and locate are not in the vLLM image (regex is), and none of them touch torch, numpy or transformers.

IMPORT PREFLIGHT. bootstrap.sh imports, immediately after the installs and before 2.8 GB of weights are fetched, every module the adapter will import: the twenty glmocr modules on the self-hosted path (leaf modules, not packages), glmocr.GlmOcr through the package's lazy __getattr__, and adapter.py under the module name arena.worker.loader gives it (arena_runtime_adapter, by spec_from_file_location). It instantiates nothing -- no GlmOcr, no detector, no CUDA context. On failure it prints '[arena] FATAL import preflight: <module>: <error>' and exits 64; on success '[arena] import preflight PASS <n> modules', recorded in the bootstrap receipt as import_preflight=PASS <n> modules. The Dockerfile runs the same list at build time. This is the check that would have caught both the wordfreq gap and the PPDocLayoutV3ImageProcessor name, neither of which the architecture preflight can see.

ARENA_LAYOUT_DIR, and why one frozen inference_config needs it. inference_config.layout_model_dir pins the BAKED path /opt/arena/weights/pp_doclayoutv3_safetensors, and it is frozen and hashed (inference_config_sha256), so it cannot hold two paths. The bootstrap path puts both checkpoints under /workspace and exports ARENA_LAYOUT_DIR -- but nothing read that variable: not adapter.py, and not arena/worker/config.py, which reads ARENA_WEIGHTS_DIR only. On bootstrap pod jdwdnvg8a2rzx6 (2026-09-03 18:34-18:39Z) vLLM initialised its engine at 18:38:17Z and the worker reported CRASHED about a minute later; adapter.load hashes the 2.65 GB checkpoint and then calls verify_layout_model, which was looking under /opt while bootstrap.sh had fetched the file to /workspace. adapter.resolve_layout_model_dir now reads ARENA_LAYOUT_DIR and falls back to inference_config, and entrypoint.sh exports the directory it just verified. The reason text was not captured on that pod, so this is the first of three load-path defects found by reading, not a confirmed root cause.

THE SDK WAS NOT ACTUALLY BEING CONFIGURED. adapter.OfficialSdkPipeline called GlmOcr(config=<dict>, layout_device=...), but 'config' is not a parameter of glmocr.api.GlmOcr.__init__ at v0.1.5: the signature is (config_path=None, *, api_key, api_url, model, mode, timeout, log_level, env_file, ocr_api_host, ocr_api_port, cuda_visible_devices, layout_device, **kwargs) and every keyword is forwarded into load_config, which drops names it does not know. So the whole dict -- maas off, ocr_api host/port, retry_max_attempts 0, task_prompt_mapping, layout model_dir -- was discarded without a word, and the shipped glmocr/config.yaml won, whose pipeline.maas.enabled is TRUE. No TypeError is raised on that path, so the adapter's TypeError guard could never fire. The adapter now renders sdk_config() to a YAML file and passes config_path=, the mechanism the SDK README's self-hosted section names, and then reads pipeline.maas.enabled, ocr_api.api_host/api_port/retry_max_attempts, layout.model_dir and page_loader.task_prompt_mapping back off GlmOcr.config_model, failing closed on any disagreement. layout_device stays a constructor keyword -- it is a real parameter and maps onto pipeline.layout.device.

NOTHING MAY REACH THE HUB ONCE THE WORKER STARTS. glmocr passes layout.model_dir straight to PPDocLayoutV3ImageProcessor.from_pretrained / PPDocLayoutV3ForObjectDetection.from_pretrained, and its shipped default for that key is the repo id PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors: a path that does not exist is read as a repo id and downloaded unpinned, replacing a hashed Apache-2.0 checkpoint with whatever main holds. The adapter refuses to construct the pipeline when the resolved layout directory does not exist, and entrypoint.sh exports HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 after both fetch steps and before the worker starts -- there, not in the image, because fetch_weights.py and fetch_layout_model.py are the two things that are allowed to download. The SDK's only other resource is a PingFang.ttf it looks for in its own package resources for layout visualisation, which falls back to PIL's default font and never fetches.

ARCHITECTURE PREFLIGHT. bootstrap.sh runs it after the import preflight and the weight fetches and before entrypoint.sh starts anything: transformers imports and its version equals the pin, 'glm_ocr' is in transformers.models.auto.configuration_auto.CONFIG_MAPPING_NAMES, the weights dir's config.json declares model_type glm_ocr, and every architecture it declares is in vllm.model_executor.models.registry.ModelRegistry.get_supported_archs(). It prints one line, '[arena] architecture preflight PASS transformers=... vllm=... arch=...', records it in /opt/arena/bootstrap-receipt.txt, and otherwise exits 64 with the reason. The Dockerfile runs the same three checks at build time. entrypoint.sh no longer exits 70 when the model server fails to become ready: it writes /opt/arena/FATAL with the reason and the last 200 lines of the server log, prints '[arena] FATAL <reason>' -- already a MODEL_LOAD signature in arena.controller.run.FATAL_LOG_SIGNATURES, retried zero times -- and sleeps, because a start command that exits is a start command RunPod restarts. The pod is then ended by the driver's D20 finally block, not by the worker's own age fuse, which never arms on that path.

PARAMETER COUNT DISCREPANCY, recorded not resolved: the card and masterplan 3.1/4 both call GLM-OCR '0.9B'. The single model.safetensors at the pinned revision is 2,650,579,464 bytes, which is about 1.3B parameters at bf16. The likely explanation is that 0.9B counts the GLM-0.5B decoder plus connector and excludes the CogViT encoder, but this lane did not verify that and does not assert it. The measured file size is what goes in the report.

VRAM BASIS: 2.65 GB of model weights plus a 133 MB layout model that shares the device by default (layout_device cuda:0), plus a 16384-token KV cache. 24 GB is a comfortable floor matching the 4090 pool masterplan 13.3 assigns. If the canary shows contention between the layout model and vLLM on one device, the SDK supports --layout-device cpu and that is the documented lever.

The card's OmniDocBench V1.5 94.62 (#1 overall) and 1.86 pages/s PDF throughput are quoted from the vendor, not reproduced. This campaign scores OmniDocBench v1.6 on its own pinned evaluator, which is a different corpus revision.

PROMPT KIND toolkit (ARENA_CONTRACT D34). GLM-OCR is prompted with a per-region task prefix, not one instruction, so the registry file for prompt_id holds a canonical rendering of the SDK's task_prompt_mapping - the ARENA_CONTRACT section 2 canonical JSON of the mapping - sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True, no trailing newline - produced by adapter.build_official_prompt_text and already written by lane R. At sdk_revision 98ef9846c7045774ff5391a50139e5cbe2850b54 that is sha256:3d62ac2e6e72a4064fdbbc5d8b045111133f663fb774e9eb0483933f36cf5e67. adapter.load hashes the mapping it hands the SDK and fails closed on any mismatch with the registry.

MIN CUDA 12.9, and why this runtime is the reason the field exists. The pinned base image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-ubuntu2404@sha256:69234fc3... declares CUDA_VERSION=12.9.1 and NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA=cuda>=12.9 in its own OCI config blob (config digest sha256:b4ff552c63bccb41898ca60b57e8f661643f34be69d6a5904e98f0fce7cfdb91, read anonymously at the pinned manifest digest on 2026-09-04; https://hub.docker.com/layers/vllm/vllm-openai/v0.19.0-ubuntu2404/images/sha256-69234fc31ff1d5e1687b2f06bba39e0f8c58dd4755f0508dbe0595cd3692b851), and the pod's own pip output showed torch 2.10.0+cu129. Pod 3xag0y00rgoj4n was placed on a host reporting cudaVersion 12.8: the architecture preflight PASSed, vLLM resolved GlmOcrMTPModel, and EngineCore then died in torch._C._cuda_init with CUDA error 804, 'forward compatibility was attempted on non supported HW', which a GeForce card cannot bridge (receipts/incidents/glm_ocr-3xag0y00rgoj4n-cuda804.json). min_cuda_version is sent as the create payload's allowedCudaVersions so RunPod cannot place this image below its own floor. glm_ocr has no provenance.json; this note is where its CUDA evidence lives.
